faqs.q: How long does a root canal treatment take?
faqs.a: Many root canals can now be finished in a single visit, but some teeth need two or more appointments, for example when the infection is severe or the canals are complex. Your dentist will decide based on the condition of the tooth, and a crown may be fitted at a later visit.

faqs.q: Is it normal to have pain after a root canal?
faqs.a: Mild soreness or tenderness when biting for a few days after a root canal is common and usually settles on its own. If the pain is severe, gets worse, or you notice swelling, go back to your dentist promptly so they can check the tooth.

faqs.q: Do I need a crown after a root canal?
faqs.a: Often, yes, especially for back teeth that take heavy chewing forces. A root canal-treated tooth can lose some strength, so dentists commonly place a crown to protect it and restore normal function. Your dentist will advise whether your tooth needs a crown or just a filling.

faqs.q: Is it better to remove the tooth than get a root canal?
faqs.a: In most cases dentists prefer to save the natural tooth with a root canal, because a properly treated and restored tooth can last for many years and keeps your bite intact. Extraction may be advised only if the tooth is too damaged to repair, and the gap then usually needs an implant, bridge or denture.
